newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close weaker on poor 10-year auction.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close weaker on poor 10-year auction.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Wednesday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds widening after a poorly received auction of 10-year Government of Canada bonds, analysts said.

"We had a weak bond auction here, with probably the biggest tail (gap between low and high yields) in a while," said Garett Prins, a fixed-income analyst with J.P. Morgan Canada. "The market has rallied quite a bit in the last few sessions and guys are generally just taking their profits." Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$1.30 to C$109.85 to yield 7.160 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 30/32 to yield 6.97 percent. The spread between the two bonds widened to 19 basis points from 17 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.

Canadian bonds fell sharply after the Canadian government said its C$2.4 billion auction of 7.25 percent bonds due June 1, 2007 average yield of 6.66 percent, with a low yield of 6.639 percent and high yield of 6.700 percent.
Adding to the weakness in Canadian bonds was a poorly received U.S. auction, which sent prices there lower as well. The U.S. Treasury this afternoon auctioned US$12 billion in 10-year notes.
"The weak auctions in the States and Canada are pretty much the main cause (of the market's decline). The dollar's weakened up a bit as well," said J.P. Morgan's Prins.
Canada's dollar weakened past C$1.38 (US$0.7246) overnight and remained there during today's session amid renewed concern among traders that U.S. interest rates could soon rise.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bonds fell C$0.95 to C$102.50 to yield 6.642 percent. The U.S. bond fell 20/32 to yield 6.76 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 12 basis points from 16 basis points on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.07 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.24 percent.
